Subject: POC Trial: Workload & Success Criteria - next steps

Hi Alicia / Ravi —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on scope and timeline.

Recap / Success criteria (from our conversation):
- Functional: Redwood must match current quality baseline on intent classification and entity extraction for clinical triage flows (sample evaluation set to be provided).
- Performance: p50 latency <= 300ms and p95 < 1.2s for the primary short-form API requests under expected load.
- Cost: target unit economics below $X per 1M tokens (we'll lock a target for the trial).
- Reliability: no more than 1% errors over a 24h window; fallbacks to smaller model if degradation observed.

POC intake items we need from Acme Health to scope the trial:
- Workload profile: average RPS, peak RPS, typical concurrency, burst characteristics (duration/frequency).
- Token profile: median & 95th percentile token length per request; example prompts (redacted).
- SLA target you want tested (latency SLO and error budget for trial).
- Network / security: IP allowlist or VPN details for Dedicated test; contact at IT for firewall rules.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: low-effort smoke + connectivity (IP allowlist, sample dataset ingestion).
- Week 2: performance tests + evaluation run against sample evaluator (we'll run loadgen and share metrics).
- Week 3: joint review and next-steps (roll to broader pilot or iterate).

Owners:
- Ben Carter (me): commercial / milestones / success criteria sign-off
- Marissa Cole (cc): CS lead during trial / evaluation
- Dylan Brooks (cc): SE / load testing and configuration

Next steps:
1) Alicia/Ravi: share workload profile and token samples (see list above).
2) IT: provide allowlist or VPN contact for connectivity.
3) Redwood: prepare draft Mutual Action Plan (attached).

I've attached a first-pass POC plan for reference [attachment: poc_plan_v1.xlsx]. Happy to jump on a short 30m sync if helpful — how does Thursday 2/18 at 10am PT look?

Thanks —

Thanks Ben — this looks good. A few answers from our side to help scope:

Success criteria confirmation:
- Functional: we'll provide a 1k-example evaluation set (de-identified) for intent/entity checks.
- Performance: target p50 <= 350ms (we can be flexible for the POC), p95 target 1s.
- Cost: we'll evaluate economics but priority is reliable latency and accuracy for triage.

Workload / traffic profile (high-level):
- Average RPS: ~5 requests/s across region during non-peak hours.
- Peak RPS: 40 requests/s during morning clinic hours (08:00–10:00 local) sustained for ~45–60 minutes.
- Concurrency: typically 20–30 concurrent requests; max observed spikes up to 120 concurrent for 2–3 minute flash periods (batch of referrals).
- Token lengths: median 120 tokens; 95th percentile ~900 tokens; max observed ~1,200 tokens for long patient narratives.
- Burst patterns: short spikes (1–3 minutes) a few times per day; larger sustained peaks tied to daily triage windows.

IT / security: I've looped in our IT alias (it-support@acmehealth.com) — they will provide firewall/IP info and a point of contact for allowlist.

Attachments/links: I'll upload the evaluation set and a small sample request log to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1AcmeHealthPOC (we'll add read-only links for Redwood).

Hi Alicia / team — quick technical follow-up from the SE side after reviewing the numbers Alicia sent. I've included a concise intake table and a few asks so we can prepare the sandbox and load tests.

Workload intake (what we need to run a representative POC load):
- Baseline RPS: 5 rps sustained (steady-state)
- Peak RPS: 40 rps sustained for 45–60m (single region)
- Typical concurrency: 20–30
- Spike concurrency: up to 120 for 2–3 minutes (occurs 1–2x/day)
- Token profile: median 120 tokens, 95th = 900, max = 1200
- Request mix: 80% short prompts (<=200 tokens), 15% mid (200–800), 5% long (>800)

Technical asks / notes:
- Model variants: we'll test two variants during the POC: a high-throughput quantized model (Q8) and a higher-quality fp16 variant. Please let us know any model constraints (for e.g., must use clinical-specialized model).
- Batchability: do you have any batching preferences or requirements? Redwood can run continuous batching; knowing if your app sends single-shot or multi-turn batches helps sizing.
- Time-window for spikes: please confirm typical local times for the morning spikes so we can schedule load tests to match production patterns.
- Network: we need either an allowlist CIDR range or a VPN endpoint; if IPs change frequently we can accommodate but prefer static allowlist for the 2-week trial window.

Proposed SE plan:
- Once IT provides allowlist/VPN and we have read-only access to the sample request logs, I'll:
  1) Provision sandbox endpoints and loadgen (2–3 instance profile candidates).
  2) Run a 2-hour performance spike (replay real request mix and token lengths).
  3) Share detailed metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, error rates, cost estimate).

We can run the initial spike as soon as this week once IT gives network access. If helpful, I'll also include a sample load script and the Redis/KV cache warm-up steps so the tests mirror production.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
